content.title: About
content.content: Cheese dip with chili pepper is a smooth spread made from processed cheese, cream and hot chili peppers. It has a creamy texture, a mild heat and a rich cheesy flavor, perfect for snacks, vegetables and chips.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cheese‑and‑chili combination has been popular in Mexican cuisine for over a century.
Chili peppers contain capsaicin, which gives the heat and may boost metabolism.
The dip is often served as a sauce for nachos because its creamy consistency holds crunchy pieces well.
Many variations exist, adding tomatoes, corn or spices such as cumin and paprika.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The cheese base provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Cheese supplies high‑quality protein that supports muscle maintenance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamins B2 and B12, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant properties of chili
items.content: Capsaicin and carotenoids in chili have antioxidant effects that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: May aid digestion
items.content: A gentle heat can stimulate gastric secretions, helping digestion.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The dip may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: Very hot versions can irritate the gastrointestinal tract, especially for those with a sensitive stomach.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because of cream and cheese, the dip is calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Prepared versions often contain added salt, which may be a concern for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve chilled as a sauce for nachos, chips, vegetable sticks, crackers, or use as a spread in sandwiches and burgers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 5‑7 days. For longer storage, freeze in small portions; thaw and stir before use.
